summary: An Owner can drag a physical group's name across several sections in one move. The drag and heading menu share packet 41's submission, busy state and read-only recovery; store::reorder_groups remains the rule owner. The accepted grid stays in place until the grouped reread succeeds.
evidence: All 44 browser_preview journeys passed in owned headless Chromium. browser_drags_group_across_sections checked the exact midpoint and one pixel below on the empty target. With the board locked, C before A sent exactly [C,A,B] at /7 and a second gesture did not submit. After commit, C [], A [59], B [61,63] had dense positions and revision 2 at /8. Releasing C on B's child row sent [A,B,C] at /8; the duplicate headings retained their original children after document reload at /9.

browser_cancels_group_heading_drag passed for (3,4) versus (6,0) displacement, Escape before and after activation, self, already-adjacent and outside releases, wrong surfaces, right button and touch. The cancelled release click was consumed, the next click was delivered, and a deliberate double-click opened the editor. Pointercancel was injected after native mouse activation. No item or group write was observed; the database snapshot stayed unchanged.

browser_scrolls_to_group_drop_target passed. With the pointer held still near the lower edge, the viewport scrolled from B to C, and the drop committed [B,C,A]. Moving away from the edge and pressing Escape stopped scrolling; leaving the visit mid-gesture and releasing did not carry the cue, marker or submission into the reopened board.

browser_recovers_group_drag_after_refusal passed. A deferred 500 left the full /7 snapshot intact before fault removal. A peer then committed [B,A,C] while the drag was held. The stale [C,A,B] at /7 received 409; Reload board only read. A deliberate [B,C,A] at /8 committed /9, followed by a 503 on refresh; retry issued only GET. A separate mid-drag demotion produced 403 and an access reread; Member and Viewer gestures sent no write, and session rejection returned to sign-in.

Fresh PostgreSQL connections compared complete item, group, board and receipt snapshots, grouped and flat readbacks on reorder, and access/session checkpoints. All 31 loopback_board_access tests and all 46 locked workspace tests passed with target-browser-packets. Workspace formatting and git diff --check passed.

The worker shell denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution. Lost POST acknowledgments and responses arriving after navigation were not separately fault-injected; the drag uses the same visit-guarded submission as the menu.
